subject: Nanotechnology
title: Peptide Self-Assembly
description: A micro-lesson that makes Peptide Self-Assembly usable.

hook.text: Short peptides — just 2 to 20 amino acids — can self-assemble into nanofibers, tubes, and hydrogels spontaneously.

buildup.text: Beta-sheet forming peptides stack through hydrogen bonds — alternating hydrophobic and hydrophilic residues drive fiber growth.

discovery.text: Peptide amphiphiles form nanofibers that mimic collagen — potential scaffolds for tissue regeneration.

twist.text: Amyloid fibrils in Alzheimer's disease are also peptide self-assembly — the same physics creates disease and cure.

climax.text: Injectable peptide hydrogels deliver drugs or cells to injury sites — self-assembling inside the body after injection.

punchline.text: A few amino acids can build nanoscale scaffolds — simplicity creates complexity.

quiz.question: How do peptide amphiphiles form nanofibers?
options: They are chemically cross-linked by an enzyme
Alternating hydrophobic and hydrophilic residues drive beta-sheet stacking through hydrogen bonds
They crystallize from solution upon evaporation
